highlights: MIT CSAIL researchers found GPT-6 Astra can natively read and write neural network weights; editing 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights raised MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%.
China's MOFCOM Announcement No. 48 proposes export restrictions on frontier model weights, and its interim pre-export registration requirement is already in effect.
OpenAI described Pando, the Git backend now behind its monorepo, while vLLM v0.33.0 and SGLang v0.5.23 shipped new releases.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra reads and writes neural network weights, MIT CSAIL finds
items.summary: MIT CSAIL researchers report that GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do from its raw weights alone, and can write small game-playing networks from scratch, without environment feedback, that outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps. Asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math without gradients, it found a weight issue causing reasoning loops and edited 0.016% of the weights, raising MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%. The authors note that editing can remove an obstacle hiding an ability but cannot add one the model lacks, which points to targeted fixes without retraining and a new angle on interpretability.

evidence.quote: Authors Rikiya Takehi * Jayden Teoh * Alex Zhang Omar Khattab Affiliations MIT CSAIL

Just by looking at the raw weights, GPT-6 Astra can tell what a network was trained to do . And without any environment feedback, it has no trouble writing, from scratch, small game-playing networks that outplay networks trained with PPO for 100 million steps.

Likewise, asked to make Qwen3.5-0.8B better at math without gradients, Astra identifies an issue in its weights causing reasoning loops that Qwen’s own model card warns about, and fixes this by natively editing 0.016% of the weights .
With the same sampling settings, this weight correction raises MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1% and generalizes out of the box to instruction following, raising IFEval by 3x.
Editing weights could remove an obstacle that hid an ability, but it could not add an ability the model lacked.

items.title: OpenAI built Pando, a Git-compatible backend for Codex-scale work
items.summary: Pando is a new backend for Git repositories that keeps compatibility with the Git protocol and client, coordinates updates to each branch independently, and reuses packfiles across fetches; it now powers all development in OpenAI's monorepo. In production it cut median push latency by nearly 5x and delivers nearly a petabyte of Git data per day. For developers, it shows how parallel agent work strains source control, and several of OpenAI's client improvements are already in upstream Git.

evidence.quote: We built Pando, a new backend for Git repositories, without interrupting any engineering work or changing how our team uses Git. Pando now powers all development in OpenAI’s monorepo.
In production, Pando cut median push latency by nearly 5x. It now delivers nearly a petabyte of Git data per day.
First, Pando coordinates updates to each branch independently. Updates to unrelated branches can proceed in parallel
Second, Pando reuses packfiles (Git’s format for compressing multiple objects together) across fetches instead of generating an individual packfile for each client.
Several of these improvements are already in upstream Git, and many others in our public repository.

items.title: China's MOFCOM Announcement No. 48 targets frontier model weights
items.summary: The announcement proposes adding 40 technologies to China's export-restriction catalogue, 23 of them in AI; weights, checkpoints, source code and architecture are restricted for models with at least 10^26 FLOPs of training compute, at least 2 trillion parameters, or a global top-10 position. The catalogue changes are still a draft, but the interim pre-export registration requirement is already in effect. API, app, web and SaaS use does not count as exporting a model and already open-sourced technology is out of scope, but deploying a restricted model locally outside China does count, so teams self-hosting Chinese models should track their suppliers' registration status.

evidence.quote: The announcement proposes adding 40 technologies to the Catalogue of Technologies Prohibited or Restricted from Export , 23 of them in artificial intelligence, and it imposes an interim pre-export registration requirement that is already in effect

Weights, key checkpoints, source code, architecture, and training and inference optimization know-how are restricted if a model meets any one of three tests: at least 10^26 FLOPs of training compute, at least 2 trillion parameters, or a global top-10 position
MOFCOM says API, app, web, SaaS, and lightweight on-device use do not count as exporting a large model. Deploying a restricted model locally outside China does count
It also excludes from management any technology that has already entered the public domain through open-source release or academic publication

items.title: OpenAI offers GPT-Rosalind-6 for biology through trusted access
items.summary: GPT-Rosalind-6 uses the same weights as GPT-6 Astra and targets biology, drug discovery and translational medicine; OpenAI offers it as GPT-Rosalind-6 Research to qualified scientists, research institutes, companies and government partners. The system card addendum reports a mean MedChemBench rubric score of 49.6%, versus 28.9% for GPT-Rosalind-5.5, and OpenAI treats the launch as High capability in the Biological and Chemical domain. Life-science teams need to apply and pass review to use it.

evidence.quote: GPT-Rosalind-6 is a frontier reasoning model for biology, drug discovery, and translational medicine. We offer it as GPT-Rosalind-6 Research to qualified scientists, research institutes, companies and government partners.
GPT-Rosalind-6 uses the same weights as GPT-6 Astra, our flagship reasoning model.
At the highest reasoning budget tested, mean rubric scores were 49.6% for GPT-Rosalind-6 and 28.9% for GPT-Rosalind-5.5.
Under our Preparedness Framework, we are treating this launch as High capability in the Biological and Chemical domain, below the threshold for Critical.

items.title: Nanbeige4.3-33B released as an open-weight agentic coding model
items.summary: Nanbeige4.3-33B is the flagship teacher model for the Nanbeige4.3 series, aimed at complex coding and professional cowork tasks, released under apache-2.0 with a context length of up to 524,288 tokens (512K). In the vendor's table it scores 80.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (Qwen3.8-27B: 73.0) and 60.3 on SWE-Bench Pro, slightly below Qwen3.8-27B's 61.7. It adds another open-weight option for agentic coding in the ~30B class, though the scores are self-reported.

evidence.quote: we first introduce Nanbeige4.3-33B, designed as the flagship teacher model for the Nanbeige4.3 series. Delivering state-of-the-art agentic performance among open models in the ~30B parameter class, Nanbeige4.3-33B excels at complex coding and professional cowork tasks
The model supports a context length of up to 524,288 tokens (512K).

items.title: Poisoning 0.1% of pretraining data plants an agent backdoor
items.summary: The authors pretrain Qwen3 models at 0.6B, 1.7B and 4B from scratch, post-train them into CLI agents, and show that poisoning only 0.1% of the pretraining corpus plants a remote code execution backdoor: the agent runs attacker-chosen commands when a trigger appears and behaves normally otherwise. Attack success rises with scale, reaching roughly 92% for the 4B model and staying positive at a 0.0005% poison rate. Anyone giving agents shell access should treat the model itself as a supply-chain risk and keep sandboxing and command review in place.

evidence.quote: We show for the first time that such poisoning can plant a remote code execution backdoor in an agent, causing it to execute attacker-chosen commands on the user's machine.

we pretrain Qwen3 models from scratch at sizes 0.6B, 1.7B, and 4B, and then post-train each into a CLI agent using a clean pipeline. Poisoning only 0.1% of the pretraining corpus with our new poison design implants the backdoor
The attack success rate (ASR) increases with model scale, with the 4B model reaching roughly 92% ASR at a 0.1% poison rate and staying positive even when the poisoning rate drops to 0.0005%.

items.title: SimpleLoRIF traces safety degradation back to fine-tuning data
items.summary: DatologyAI researchers present SimpleLoRIF, which simplifies a low-rank attribution method and restricts backpropagation to the final four transformer blocks so it can embed datasets on the order of a million examples and flag fine-tuning examples whose gradients align with unsafe behavior. Removing the 20% most aligned examples from Tulu 3 yields SafeTulu, which reduces GCG attack success rate by up to 22% across Qwen, Llama and Olmo while largely preserving capability. Teams can use the approach to filter benign-looking data that erodes safety before fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: Submitted by Pratyush Maini on Nov 2 · DatologyAI
By simplifying a low-rank attribution method and restricting backpropagation to the final four transformer blocks , SimpleLoRIF can embed datasets on the order of a million examples

We then use SimpleLoRIF to build SafeTulu , a version of Tulu 3 with the 20% of examples most gradient-aligned with unsafe responses removed. Training on SafeTulu reduces GCG attack success rate by up to 22% across Qwen, Llama, and Olmo

items.title: ServiceNow releases Apriel Voice 27B Preview, an open speech model
items.summary: Built on the post-trained Gemma 4 26B-A4B checkpoint, Apriel Voice 27B Preview processes speech directly and generates both responses and tool calls without a separate dialogue model, while keeping text and image input. In thinking mode it scores 98.90 on Big Bench Audio and 81.13 on Speech-BFCL, with a 65.51% task success rate on τ-Voice and a mean latency of 1.91 seconds. Developers building tool-using voice assistants can start from a single model, with weights listed on Hugging Face.

evidence.quote: Built on the post-trained Gemma 4 26B-A4B checkpoint, Apriel Voice directly processes speech and generates both responses and tool calls without requiring a separate dialogue model.
In thinking mode, Apriel Voice achieves a score of 98.90 on Big Bench Audio , 81.13 on Speech-BFCL , and a task success rate of 65.51% on τ-Voice , with a mean latency of 1.91 seconds.

items.title: vLLM v0.33.0 moves to PyTorch 2.14 and CUDA 13.0-only builds
items.summary: vLLM v0.33.0 brings 927 commits from 389 contributors, support for new models such as Reflection Beam-1.0 (501B MoE, 23B active) and Step-5 Preview, and an upgrade to PyTorch 2.14.0. CUDA 12.9 wheels and images are no longer published, leaving CUDA 13.0 artifacts only, and every image is also published under the shorter vllm/vllm name. Deployments still on CUDA 12.9 need to move to CUDA 13.0 before upgrading.

items.title: SGLang v0.5.23 runs oversized MoE models on a single consumer GPU
items.summary: SGLang v0.5.23 merges 1007 PRs from 257 contributors: opt-in Paged Experts runs MoE models larger than GPU memory on a single consumer GPU, up to 30x faster than CPU offload; DeepSeek-V4.1 on GB300 gets up to 1.5x more prefill throughput; and a low-latency mode makes single-user DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash decode up to 44% faster on GB300 and 75% on MI350X. It also runs on Google TPU7x through SGLang-TorchTPU. Running large MoE models locally now has a faster option than CPU offload.

items.title: vercel-labs open-sources agent-desktop for accessibility-tree computer use
items.summary: agent-desktop is a CLI and C library that lets agents read and operate desktop apps on macOS, Windows and Linux through the OS accessibility tree: each snapshot returns JSON with a ref for every actionable element, and the agent acts on a ref and snapshots again, with no pixel matching. It installs with npm install -g agent-desktop and is licensed Apache-2.0. It gives agents a structured alternative to screenshot-based desktop control.

evidence.quote: Computer use for AI agents: read and operate desktop apps through the OS accessibility tree. A CLI and C library for macOS, Windows and Linux. A snapshot returns JSON with a ref for every element an agent can act on.
Install on macOS, Windows or Linux with npm: npm install -g agent-desktop
License Apache-2.0

items.title: Anthropic's amended S-1 shows about $17B in Q3 revenue
items.summary: Anthropic's amended S-1 reports roughly $17 billion in third-quarter revenue, up about 1,127% year over year but only around 47% quarter over quarter, a $23.29 billion quarterly net loss, and about $895.4 billion in purchase and lease commitments.

evidence.quote: During its third quarter, Anthropic generated roughly $17 billion in revenue, up about 1,127% from the same period last year. Revenue growth slowed on a quarter-to-quarter basis, however. Third-quarter revenue increased around 47%
The company reported a net loss of $23.29 billion during its third quarter.
In the amended S-1, Anthropic said it has entered into purchase commitments and lease agreements with an aggregate committed spend of about $895.4 billion
